uploads/science/Scipad/Year 9 Book 1/Ans.searchText: INTRODUCTION TO THE LABORATORY Variables A variable is something that can affect the results of an experiment. When carrying out an experiment, all the variables (except the one you are testing) should be kept the same (these are called ‘control variables’). Controlling these variables ensures your test is ‘fair’. The variable you are testing is called the ‘independent variable’ and is the only one that should be changed during an investigation.
